rows.subtype: Following with the eyes and joint attention [Expressing]
rows.description: A toddler tracks a caregiver with the eyes and looks where a parent points, sharing attention on an object. Steady following shows interest and trust, and early lack of it may be worth discussing with a paediatrician.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: interest, trust

rows.description: A toddler turns the eyes away from an overwhelming, loud or intense interaction to calm down. It is a self-soothing break, not rejection, and adults can lower the intensity.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: calm, overwhelm

rows.subtype: Puffed cheeks and cheek raising in play [Expressing]
rows.description: A toddler puffs the cheeks in imitation games or raises the cheeks in a big smile, showing fun and copying skills. These playful movements show growing control of the face.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: playfulness

rows.subtype: Wrinkled nose at smells and tastes [Expressing]
rows.description: A toddler wrinkles the nose at a bad smell or unfamiliar food, a reflex-like sign of disgust or dislike. Adults can respect it without forcing food and try again later.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: admiration, disgust

rows.description: A toddler puckers the lips for a kiss, sucks them in when concentrating or stretches them in a squeal of excitement. These are exploratory and social, with meaning shifting by context.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: excitement

rows.description: A toddler's lower lip trembles or turns down before crying, signalling sadness, hurt or overwhelm. A soothing voice and closeness usually help.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: sadness, overwhelm, hurt

rows.description: A toddler stares with the jaw dropped in wonder or while concentrating, and drools while teething. It shows attention or discomfort, not disrespect.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: admiration, curiosity, awe

rows.subtype: Sticking out the tongue in play and taste [Expressing]
rows.description: A toddler sticks out the tongue while imitating, tasting or being silly, meaning play or mild disgust. It is not rude at this age, and adults can copy it playfully.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: playfulness, disgust

rows.description: A toddler goes blank or still when overwhelmed, tired or in a new place, a shutdown rather than calm. Gentle closeness and reducing stimulation help.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: tiredness, calm, overwhelm

rows.subtype: Relaxed face in sleep and comfort [Expressing]
rows.description: A toddler's relaxed face while feeding or drifting to sleep shows comfort and safety. A very still, unresponsive face while awake is worth a caregiver's attention.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: calm, trust
